links.outcome: Expert-rated quality of clinician-edited LLM drafts versus unedited LLM drafts and clinician-only documents
links.effect: Overall quality (0-10) for discharge summaries: clinician-in-the-loop 7.8, clinician-only 6.9, LLM-only 6.0; referrals: 8.0, 6.8, 5.3. LLM-only consistently lowest scores across most domains.
links.quote: The LLM-only group consistently received the lowest scores across most domains for both discharge summaries and discharge referrals; however, in the discharge summaries, the Possibility of Harm and Validity for Clinical Use domains, and in the discharge referrals, the Possibility of Harm domain, achieved scores comparable to those of the Clinician-only group ( Fig 5 ).

links.outcome: Quality of AI drafts after clinician verification and editing versus unedited drafts
links.effect: Clinician-in-the-loop drafts scored higher than LLM-only in nearly all quality domains and overall quality (summaries 7.8 vs 6.0; referrals 8.0 vs 5.3).
links.quote: The Clinician-in-the-loop group showed higher average scores than the Clinician-only group across nearly all domains in discharge summaries and discharge referrals.

links.outcome: Human-AI team documentation time and quality versus clinician-only and standalone LLM
links.effect: Time not significantly different in primary analysis (summaries β=-59.4 s, p=.18; referrals β=52.9 s, p=.08); overall quality higher with clinician-in-the-loop (referrals β=1.17, p=.004).
links.quote: In the primary analysis, the Clinician-in-the-loop group had a significantly higher overall quality score than the Clinician-only group for discharge referrals.

links.outcome: AI performance as used by clinicians in workflow versus standalone LLM output
links.effect: Clinician-edited LLM drafts outperformed LLM-only and clinician-only drafts on overall quality; LLM-only fastest but lowest quality.
links.quote: Clinician-edited LLM drafts generally achieved higher scores than manually drafted documents across most quality domains and overall quality ratings.

links.outcome: Documentation time and quality of LLM-assisted documentation versus manual drafting
links.effect: Time: summaries β=-59.4 s (p=.18), referrals β=52.9 s (p=.08) in primary LMM; quality generally higher with clinician-in-the-loop.
links.quote: Clinician-in-the-loop showed a shorter creation time for summaries (β = -59.4 seconds; 95% CI, -150.6 to 31.7; P = .18) and a longer creation time for referrals (β = 52.9 seconds; 95% CI, -7.0 to 112.9; P = .08) than Clinician-only, although neither difference was statistically significant.

screen.practice: clinician-in-the-loop review and editing of LLM drafts
screen.reason: This randomized controlled trial evaluated the effect of a clinician-in-the-loop review workflow compared to unedited LLM drafts and clinician-only drafting on documentation time and quality using simulated patient records.
